dialogue.origin: 〈よろしくお願いします。〉
dialogue.content: Pleased to meet you.

dialogue.origin: はじめまして　おはようございます
dialogue.content: Nice to meet you. Good morning.

dialogue.origin: あと２分ありますが　もう始めていいかんじでしょうか？
dialogue.content: We still have two minutes, but would it be alright to start now?

dialogue.origin: 大丈夫です。
dialogue.content: Yes, that's fine.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございます
dialogue.content: Thank you.

dialogue.origin: では始めたいと思います　よろしくお願い致します
dialogue.content: Alright, let's get started then. I look forward to our session.

dialogue.origin: （よろしくお願いします）
dialogue.content: (I look forward to it as well.)

dialogue.origin: さっそくですが　相談員です　あなたの性別と今日はどのような用件でいらいたかお聴かせ頂けますか？
dialogue.content: To begin, I'm the counselor. May I ask your gender and what brings you here today?

dialogue.origin: よろしくお願いします。女性です。
dialogue.content: Thank you. I'm female.

dialogue.origin: 息子との関係で悩んでいます
dialogue.content: I'm struggling with my relationship with my son.

dialogue.origin: 女性ですね　ありがとうございます
dialogue.content: You're female. Thank you for sharing.

dialogue.origin: 息子さんとの関係でお悩みなんですね
dialogue.content: So you're concerned about your relationship with your son.

dialogue.origin: はい。
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: もう少し詳しくお聴かせ頂けますか？
dialogue.content: Could you please tell me a bit more about it?

dialogue.origin: 息子が働きません。家でゲームばかりしています
dialogue.content: My son won't work. He just stays at home and plays games all the time.

dialogue.origin: お子さんは何歳の方でしょうか？
dialogue.content: How old is your son?

dialogue.origin: 28歳です
dialogue.content: He's 28 years old.

dialogue.origin: 28歳の息子さんが働いてくれずゲームばかりしているのですね　それは心配になってしまいますよね
dialogue.content: So your 28-year-old son isn't working and just plays games all day. That must be worrying for you.

dialogue.origin: 今まで働いたことはあったのでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Has he ever worked before?

dialogue.origin: はい。新卒で会社に入ったのですが、半年で辞めてしまいその後今に至ります。
dialogue.content: Yes. He joined a company right after graduation, but he quit after six months and hasn't worked since.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね　半年で辞めてしまった理由は聴いていますか？
dialogue.content: I see. Have you heard why he quit after just six months?

dialogue.origin: 会社が合わないとは言っていましたが、それ以上のことは聞いても話してくれません。
dialogue.content: He said the company wasn't a good fit, but he won't tell me anything more, even when I ask.

dialogue.origin: 聞いても話してくれないのは困りますよね
dialogue.content: It must be difficult when he won't talk to you even when you ask.

dialogue.origin: ええ。。。
dialogue.content: Yes...

dialogue.origin: その会社は第一志望とかで好きで入った会社ですか？そういうのはなく　とりあえず入れたから入ったかんじでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Was it a company he was passionate about joining, perhaps his first choice? Or was it more of a situation where he took the first job he could get?

dialogue.origin: その辺りは詳しくは聞いていません。ただ、入社前は楽しそうにしていたので、心配していなかったです。
dialogue.content: I haven't heard the details about that. But he seemed excited before he started, so I wasn't worried.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね　失礼な質問になってしまうかもしれませんが息子さんは学生時代に登校拒否などの経験はありましたか？
dialogue.content: I see. This may be a sensitive question, but did your son ever have issues like school refusal when he was a student?

dialogue.origin: ありません。
dialogue.content: No, he didn't.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね　ではその頃の癖で…とかはないようですし何があったか不安ですよね。
dialogue.content: I see. So it doesn't seem to be a recurring pattern from back then. It must make you even more anxious about what could have happened.

dialogue.origin: 息子さんとの関係で今一番困っている事はありますか？
dialogue.content: What is the most difficult thing for you right now in your relationship with your son?

dialogue.origin: あれば差し支えない範囲でかまわないのでお聴かせ願えますか？
dialogue.content: If there is, could you please share it with me, to the extent that you're comfortable?

dialogue.origin: そうですね。働いてくれないことと、なぜなのかを話してくれないことでしょうか。。。家での会話は普通なのですが、仕事のことになると部屋に凝ってしまいます。
dialogue.content: Let's see. I suppose it's the fact that he won't work, and that he won't tell me why. We can talk normally at home, but as soon as the topic of work comes up, he retreats to his room.

dialogue.origin: それは余計に会社での半年の間に何があったか気になりますよね
dialogue.content: That must make you even more curious about what happened during those six months at the company.

dialogue.origin: はい。
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: ゲームはどのようなゲームをしているかわかりますか？
dialogue.content: Do you know what kinds of games he's playing?

dialogue.origin: わかりません。部屋には入れてくれないので。
dialogue.content: I don't know. He won't let me in his room.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね　例えば格闘ものとかであればストレスがたまっているけど吐き出し口がなくて、とかかなと思って聴いてみました。ありがとうございます。
dialogue.content: I see. I was just wondering if they were, for example, fighting games, which might suggest he's stressed and has no outlet for it. Thank you for sharing.

dialogue.origin: いえ、わからなくてすみません。
dialogue.content: No, I'm sorry I don't know.

dialogue.origin: いま教えて下さったこと以外の事で何か気付いた点や気になった事はありますか？
dialogue.content: Is there anything else you've noticed or been concerned about, besides what you've already told me?

dialogue.origin: なにしろ、仕事についてもらわないと、息子の将来が心配です。いつまでも養っていけるわけではないので。。。
dialogue.content: Above all, I'm worried about my son's future if he doesn't get a job. I can't support him forever...

dialogue.origin: そうですよね
dialogue.content: I understand.

dialogue.origin: 息子さんはゲームばかりとのことですが時々でも外に出掛ける事はないのですか？
dialogue.content: You mentioned your son only plays games, but does he ever go out, even occasionally?

dialogue.origin: 私が日中仕事をしているので、いない間に出かけているのかはわかりません。私がいる間はコンビニくらいは行っているようですが
dialogue.content: I work during the day, so I don't know if he goes out while I'm gone. When I'm home, he seems to go to the convenience store at least.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね　でもコンビニは行かれてるのですね
dialogue.content: I see. So he does go to the convenience store.

dialogue.origin: コンビニに行ってくる、といって出ていくので、そう思っていますが、本当はどこに行っているかはわからないです。
dialogue.content: He says, "I'm going to the convenience store," and leaves, so that's what I assume, but I don't really know where he's going.

dialogue.origin: なるほど　それも気になりますよね
dialogue.content: I see. That must be another concern for you.

dialogue.origin: はい。でもつけるわけにもいかないので。。。
dialogue.content: Yes. But I can't exactly follow him...

dialogue.origin: それからひなたさんに関しては病気などはあるのでしょうか？さきほど「いつまでも養っていけるわけではないので」とあったので少し気になりました。
dialogue.content: And regarding yourself, Ms. Hinata, do you have any illnesses? I'm asking because you mentioned earlier that you "can't support him forever," which made me a little concerned.

dialogue.origin: つけたい気持ちにはなってしまいますよね
dialogue.content: And it's understandable to feel like you want to follow him.

dialogue.origin: いえ、病気はないです。と、思っていますが、、、何か病気っぽいですか？
dialogue.content: No, I don't have any illnesses—or at least I don't think so... Do I seem unwell somehow?

dialogue.origin: 内緒で仕事を探してるとかならいいですよね
dialogue.content: It would be nice if he were secretly looking for a job, wouldn't it?

dialogue.origin: そうですね。
dialogue.content: Yes, that would be nice.

dialogue.origin: いえ　みんな共通の「親はいつまでも生きてない」というものかと思ったのですが一応念のため　病気を持ってるケースもあるので聴いてみました
dialogue.content: No, not at all. I thought you might have been referring to the common sentiment that "parents won't be around forever," but I just wanted to ask to be sure, as some clients do have health conditions.

dialogue.origin: ああ、そうなのですね。不安になりました。
dialogue.content: Oh, I see. You had me worried for a moment.

dialogue.origin: ひなたさんが病気っぽいとかは感じていませんよ　変な質問だったようでごめんなさい
dialogue.content: I don't have the impression that you seem ill at all, Ms. Hinata. I'm sorry if that was a strange question.

dialogue.origin: いえ。それならよかったです。
dialogue.content: Not at all. I'm relieved to hear that.

dialogue.origin: でも本当に困りましたよね
dialogue.content: But it's truly a difficult situation, isn't it?

dialogue.origin: はい・・・。どうしたらいいでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Yes... What should I do?

dialogue.origin: ゲーム以外で息子さんが好きな事や興味がある事はありますか？
dialogue.content: Besides games, are there other things your son likes or is interested in?

dialogue.origin: そうですね、昔は野球をやっていましたが、今はやっている感じではないですね。
dialogue.content: Well, he used to play baseball, but it doesn't seem like he does now.

dialogue.origin: テレビで試合を見ていることはありますが
dialogue.content: He does watch games on TV sometimes, though.

dialogue.origin: なるほど
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: 習い事とかは何かしてましたか？なにか得意な事とかを仕事に出来ればと考えたのですが…
dialogue.content: Did he take any lessons? I was thinking perhaps he could turn something he's good at into a job...

dialogue.origin: 学生の時は塾と草野球くらいでしょうか。
dialogue.content: When he was a student, I think it was just cram school and amateur baseball.

dialogue.origin: 野球が好きなんですね
dialogue.content: So he likes baseball.

dialogue.origin: 好きなんだとおもいます。
dialogue.content: I think so.

dialogue.origin: 例えば草野球の監督とか仕事には？
dialogue.content: What about a job like managing an amateur baseball team?

dialogue.origin: 草野球の監督ってちゃんとした収入になるのでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Can you make a proper living as an amateur baseball manager?

dialogue.origin: 町内会のとかならプロじゃなくても出来るみたいですよ　収入はわかりませんが私のいとこのお兄ちゃんがやっていて聴いたことがあったので提案してみました
dialogue.content: It seems you don't have to be a professional for something like a neighborhood team. I'm not sure about the income, but my cousin's older brother does it, and I heard about it from him, so I thought I'd suggest it.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね。
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: お兄ちゃんは子供相手にだそうですがとても楽しく話してました　生き甲斐的な　何か楽しみを見つけられると元ベーションにつながって普通の仕事にまた興味が湧くかなって思ったのですが、どう思いますか？
dialogue.content: He apparently works with children, and he spoke about it with such joy. It's like his purpose in life. I thought that if your son could find something enjoyable, it might motivate him and spark his interest in a regular job again. What do you think?

dialogue.origin: そうかもしれないですね。
dialogue.content: That might be true.

dialogue.origin: それを息子に私から提案する、ということでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Are you suggesting that I propose that to my son?

dialogue.origin: なにか息子さんはやりがい、刺激を探してるのかなと思いました。
dialogue.content: I thought perhaps your son is looking for some kind of purpose or stimulation.

dialogue.origin: できればやりたいことを自分で見つけてほしいと思っています。
dialogue.content: If possible, I'd prefer for him to find what he wants to do on his own.

dialogue.origin: 草野球の監督にかぎらず　なにか刺激になるものをすすめるのはいいかもしれませんね？
dialogue.content: It doesn't have to be managing a baseball team, but suggesting something stimulating might be a good idea, don't you think?

dialogue.origin: 刺激、ですか。たとえばどんなことでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Stimulation? Like what, for example?

dialogue.origin: そうですよね　自分で見つけるのが私も一番かと思います
dialogue.content: That's true. I also think it's best if he finds it himself.

dialogue.origin: なんでもいいと思います例えばテレビで野球は見てるとの事なので　野球以外の番組を見てる時に
dialogue.content: I think it could be anything. For example, you mentioned he watches baseball on TV, so when he's watching other shows...

dialogue.origin: 笑ったり真剣に見てる時があれば　笑った時にどう感じて面白かった？こうだったよねとか
dialogue.content: If there are moments when he laughs or watches intently, when he laughs you could ask, 'What did you find funny?' or reflect, 'It was because of this, wasn't it?'

dialogue.origin: なにに対して真剣になってたかとか
dialogue.content: Or what he was so serious about.

dialogue.origin: ひなたさんがよく見て気付いた点を話してあげるのはどうでしょうか？
dialogue.content: How about observing closely and sharing what you notice with him, Ms. Hinata?

dialogue.origin: 少しづつ仕事のことも話してくれるかもしれません
dialogue.content: He might gradually start opening up about work as well.

dialogue.origin: はじめのほうで　入る前は楽しそうだった　会社が合わないと言ってたとあったので
dialogue.content: Since you mentioned at the beginning that he seemed happy before starting, but then said the company wasn't a good fit.

dialogue.origin: そうですね・・・。私もここ数年でやれることはやってきているのですが、なかなか仕事をするところまで行かないので、困っています。草野球の監督は思いつかなかったですが、、、。
dialogue.content: That's right... I've been doing what I can these past few years, but it never leads to him getting a job, so I'm at a loss. I had never thought of him managing a recreational baseball team, though.

dialogue.origin: まずは会社が嫌なのか、仕事をするのが嫌なのか、だと思って、南海か聞いているんですけど、そういう話は聞いてくれないんです。返事もなく部屋にこもってしまいます。
dialogue.content: First, I thought I should find out if he dislikes that specific company, or if he dislikes the idea of working in general, so I've asked him many times, but he won't listen to that kind of talk. He just goes to his room without answering.

dialogue.origin: いきなり仕事～！と食い込むのは危険かもしれません　はじめは周りからいろいろ触れて行って少しづつでかまわないと思います
dialogue.content: Pushing the topic of work on him directly might be risky. I think it's better to start by touching on related topics and taking it one small step at a time.

dialogue.origin: よっぽど辛い事があったのでしょうね
dialogue.content: Something very painful must have happened.

dialogue.origin: たぶんまだ自分自身答えがわからないのかもしれませんね
dialogue.content: He probably doesn't know the answer himself yet.

dialogue.origin: そうなのかもしれません。会社が嫌なら違う会社ではたらいてくれればいいんですけど。アルバイトでもいいので。
dialogue.content: That might be the case. If he hated that company, I wish he would just work at a different one. Even a part-time job would be fine.

dialogue.origin: いま一生懸命悩んで探して　ゲームも多分それを見つけるため　心を落ち着かせるためにやってるのかもしれません、その点はどう思いますか？
dialogue.content: He might be struggling and searching right now, and perhaps the games are a way for him to find an answer or to calm his mind. What do you think about that possibility?

dialogue.origin: 何かを考えているようにはみえないんですよね。
dialogue.content: He doesn't look like he's thinking about anything.

dialogue.origin: そうですよね　そう思いますよね
dialogue.content: I understand. It's natural to feel that way.

dialogue.origin: はい。何も考えていないようにしか見えないので
dialogue.content: Yes. It just looks like he's not thinking about anything at all.

dialogue.origin: こちらとしては不安ばかりになってしまいます
dialogue.content: It just makes me more and more anxious.

dialogue.origin: 何も考えてないようにわざと見せてるのかも？
dialogue.content: Perhaps he's intentionally making it look like he's not thinking?

dialogue.origin: そうなのでしょうか。なんのためにでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Could that be? Why would he do that?

dialogue.origin: トラウマ的なものがあるとしても息子さんのプライド的なものがあって恥ずかしいとか
dialogue.content: Even if there's something traumatic, it could be a matter of pride for him, and he might feel embarrassed.

dialogue.origin: 自分でなんとかしたいって気持ちがあるとか
dialogue.content: Or a desire to handle it on his own.

dialogue.origin: 5年も悩んでいるのでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Would he really be struggling with this for five years?

dialogue.origin: 言われて立ち上がるのが嫌っ！みたいな？
dialogue.content: Like, he doesn't want to get back on his feet just because someone told him to?

dialogue.origin: まだ28歳なので5年くらいは悩んでしまう事もあるかと思いますよ
dialogue.content: He's still only 28. It's not unusual for someone to struggle with something for five years at that age.

dialogue.origin: そうですかね・・・。
dialogue.content: You think so...?

dialogue.origin: まだ若いですし
dialogue.content: He's still young.

dialogue.origin: 男性として思う部分があるのかもしれませんね
dialogue.content: There might be certain things he feels as a man.

dialogue.origin: 息子さんは一人っ子ですか？
dialogue.content: Is your son an only child?

dialogue.origin: はい。一人っ子です
dialogue.content: Yes, he's an only child.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: ひなたさんの旦那さん　息子さんのお父様はお仕事などされてますか？
dialogue.content: Does your husband, your son's father, work?

dialogue.origin: はい。普通のサラリーマンです
dialogue.content: Yes. He's a regular office worker.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね　息子さんはお父さんのようになりたい！同じ仕事をしたい！とかは？
dialogue.content: I see. Does your son ever say things like, "I want to be like my dad!" or "I want to do the same job!"?

dialogue.origin: 小さいときは言っていたかもしれませんが、今は主人ともほとんど話しをしていません。
dialogue.content: He might have said that when he was little, but now he barely speaks to my husband.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね　息子さんはお父さんのようになりたい！同じ仕事をしたい！などは？
dialogue.content: I see. What about things like, "I want to be like my dad!" or "I want to do the same job!"?

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: そういうことを言っているのは、聞いたことがありませんね。
dialogue.content: I've never heard him say anything like that.

dialogue.origin: 家族会議的なことは部屋にこもるようになる前に出来たことはありますか？
dialogue.content: Were you able to have any family meetings before he started shutting himself in his room?

dialogue.origin: 家族会議ですか。。うちはあまりやってこなかったですね。3人なので、普通に食卓で話していましたから。
dialogue.content: Family meetings...? We didn't really do that. Since there are only three of us, we would just talk normally at the dinner table.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね息子さんとお父さんは話せてないようですが　ひなたさんは旦那さんと息子さんの事について深く話す事はありますか？
dialogue.content: I see. It sounds like your son and his father aren't talking, but do you and your husband have in-depth conversations about your son?

dialogue.origin: 会社を辞めた時には3人で話すこともあったり、主人と2人で話すこともありましたが、ここ2年は相談しても放っておけ、というだけです
dialogue.content: When he quit his job, the three of us would sometimes talk, and my husband and I would talk, but for the last two years, whenever I try to discuss it, he just says, "Leave him alone."

dialogue.origin: お父さんは諦めてしまっているかんじでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Does it seem like his father has given up?

dialogue.origin: そうかもしれないですね。
dialogue.content: That might be the case.

dialogue.origin: あ　すみません　そろそろ時間が迫って来てしまいました　少しまとめに入らせて頂きたいと思いますが今まで話してみて気付いた点や、何かありますか？
dialogue.content: Oh, I'm sorry, but our time is almost up. I'd like to start wrapping things up, but after talking today, is there anything you've noticed or realized?

dialogue.origin: はい、お願いします
dialogue.content: Yes, please.

dialogue.origin: 気づいた点は、とくになかったです
dialogue.content: I haven't really noticed anything in particular.

dialogue.origin: まだ言えなかった　話してないことなどありますか？
dialogue.content: Is there anything else you haven't had a chance to say?

dialogue.origin: いえ、大丈夫です
dialogue.content: No, I'm fine.

dialogue.origin: 時間になりましたので終了で大丈夫でしょうか？まだもう少し話したいなどあれば延長しても大丈夫ですよ。
dialogue.content: Our time is up, so shall we end here? If you'd like to talk a little more, we can extend the session.

dialogue.origin: 少しでもお役に立てていればいいのですが・・・
dialogue.content: I hope I was able to help, even just a little...

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございました
dialogue.content: Thank you very much.

dialogue.origin: 終了で大丈夫ですか？
dialogue.content: So you're okay with ending the session now?

dialogue.origin: はい。
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: （おつかれさまでした。ありがとうございました）
dialogue.content: (Thank you for your time. Thank you very much.)

dialogue.origin: 了解しました　ありがとうございました
dialogue.content: Understood. Thank you very much.

dialogue.origin: また機会があればよろしくお願い致します
dialogue.content: I hope to speak with you again if the opportunity arises.

dialogue.origin: おつかれさまでした
dialogue.content: Thank you for your time.

dialogue.origin: では失礼します
dialogue.content: Goodbye then.

topic.sub: 息子とのコミュニケーションの問題
